span: several such evidences taken together may carry enough probative force to justify the conviction
why: Court's own statement that accumulated circumstantial evidence forming an unbroken chain can justify conviction.

span: the appellant’s conviction deserves to be upheld
why: Headnote holding: a conviction based on circumstantial evidence is upheld because the prosecution proved an unbroken chain.

span: Links in the chain of circumstances is necessary to be established for conviction on the basis of circumstantial evidence
why: Headnote states the requirement of an established chain and holds it unmet (suspicion is not proof), setting aside the conviction.

span: reiterated when conviction on the basis of circumstantial evidence can be maintained
why: Court introduces and relies on the Padala Veera Reddy tests as stating when a conviction on circumstantial evidence can be maintained.

span: to convict an accused on the basis of circumstantial evidence, the prosecution must prove beyond reasonable doubt each of the incriminating circumstances on which it proposes to rely
why: Headnote states the conditions for conviction on circumstantial evidence and upholds the High Court's setting aside of a conviction because they were unmet.

span: As to when on strength of evidence circumstantial in nature conviction can be lawfully sustained, the law is well settled
why: Headnote states the settled principles under which a conviction on circumstantial evidence can be lawfully sustained.
